stories.headline: AMD acquires AI memory optimization startup MEXT to ease data center DRAM crunch

key_facts.fact: AMD announced on June 15 the acquisition of MEXT, a startup specializing in AI-driven memory optimization technology for data center infrastructure.
MEXT has developed AI-powered predictive memory technology that makes flash storage behave more like DRAM, expanding usable memory capacity while reducing infrastructure costs.
Financial terms were not disclosed; analysts characterize the deal as small, but AMD says MEXT's technology will be integrated across its data center portfolio.
Dan McNamara, AMD's senior vice president and general manager of compute and enterprise, said integrating MEXT's tech is part of expanding AMD's full-stack compute and AI offerings.
Memory has become a critical constraint across cloud and enterprise environments as AI models, data analytics, virtualization and HPC workloads grow in complexity.

stories.headline: Anthropic senior staff meet Trump officials on Fable/Mythos export controls; no resolution

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's senior tech staff Logan Graham, Dave Orr and Nicholas Carlini met Commerce Department officials in Washington on June 15 to discuss the export-control directive blocking Fable 5 and Mythos 5, with additional meetings scheduled at the CIA and with White House science adviser Michael Kratsios.

After the Monday meeting, a person close to the talks said the parties are not yet discussing lifting the restrictions, and Anthropic's spokesperson said both sides are 'working quickly to get this resolved.'

A White House official told Axios that Amazon CEO Andy Jassy raised concerns to senior Trump officials about security risks in Anthropic's latest models, and a White House source said Anthropic's initial position was 'no, we're not going to do anything, this is not a real issue.'

CNBC reported the Commerce directive was issued Friday June 12 at 1:00 p.m. ET by phone and confirmed at 5:30 p.m. ET by formal letter, ordering Anthropic to suspend access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 'by any foreign national, whether inside or outside the United States.'
Anthropic announced Fable 5 and Mythos 5 on Tuesday June 9 and had worked with government agencies to test the models pre-release with approval to deploy, per a person familiar with the discussions.

stories.headline: Bank of Japan raises rates to 1%, highest since 1995, citing Iran war oil shock

key_facts.fact: BOJ voted 7-1 to raise its short-term policy rate to 1.0% from 0.75%, the highest level since 1995 and first hike since December 2025.
Board member Toichiro Asada, the first member hand-picked by dovish premier Sanae Takaichi, dissented, arguing downside growth risks from the Middle East conflict outweighed inflation risks.
BOJ flagged upside inflation risk, citing faster-than-expected pass-through of oil prices into consumer prices, and projected underlying CPI clearly above 2% target.
Japan's wholesale inflation spiked to a three-year high of 6.3% in May; yen-based import prices jumped 25.5%.
Nikkei 225 hit a fresh record after the decision; yen briefly firmed before giving back gains as investors took comfort the BOJ avoided a 50bp move.
Japan reportedly spent ¥11.7 trillion ($73.5 billion) on yen intervention in May; yen had touched 160 against the dollar and languished there most of June.

stories.headline: DeepSeek closes $7.4B first round at $50B+ valuation via LP run by Liang Wenfeng

key_facts.fact: Chinese AI lab DeepSeek raised more than 50 billion yuan ($7.4 billion) at a valuation exceeding $50 billion in its first outside funding round, per The Information.
Investors had to put capital into a limited partnership managed by DeepSeek CEO Liang Wenfeng rather than directly into DeepSeek, with a five-year lock-up and no voting rights.
China's National Artificial Intelligence Industry Investment Fund is the sole exception, investing directly in DeepSeek with voting rights and no lock-up.

Founder Liang committed 20 billion yuan of his own money to the round; Tencent is considering 10 billion yuan and battery giant CATL is considering 5 billion yuan, which would make them the largest external investors.
Until this round DeepSeek had taken no external venture capital, funded entirely from the balance sheet of High-Flyer, Liang's quantitative hedge fund.

organizations: China's National Artificial Intelligence Industry Investment Fund

stories.headline: DOJ files brief defending xAI's unpermitted gas turbines as vital to US military

key_facts.fact: The Department of Justice intervened on Monday, June 15, in the NAACP lawsuit over xAI's gas turbines, asking the court to dismiss the case alongside xAI and the state of Mississippi.
The DOJ filing argues that stopping the turbines 'threatens American national, economic, and energy security' by cutting off power for AI 'that supports the Department of War's military operations.'
A declaration from Cameron Stanley, the DoD's chief digital and AI officer, says Grok's Gov model supports 'vital national security missions,' including recent US strikes against Iran.
The DOJ memorandum states there are only four AI models, including Grok, that 'support mission-critical operations across Secret and Top-Secret classified networks.'

The NAACP suit, filed April 14, 2026, alleges xAI is operating unpermitted natural gas turbines at its Colossus 2 data center in Southaven, Mississippi, violating the Clean Air Act and endangering nearby communities.
Southern Environmental Law Center records show 57 turbines were operating without permits at the Colossus 2 site as of mid-May; many were added after the NAACP filed suit.

stories.headline: FDA approves first PD-1/HIF-2α combo (Keytruda + Welireg) for high-risk kidney cancer

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved Merck's Welireg (belzutifan) in combination with Keytruda (pembrolizumab) as adjuvant treatment for adults with renal cell carcinoma with a clear cell component at intermediate-high or high risk of recurrence after nephrectomy.
Merck said the decision marks the first approval of PD-1 and hypoxia-inducible factor-2 alpha (HIF-2α) inhibitor combination regimens.
Approval is based on the Phase III LITESPARK-022 trial including 1,841 participants, led by Toni Choueiri of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.
With median 28.4-month follow-up, the combination cut the risk of recurrence, metastasis or death by 28%; about 81% on the regimen were cancer-free at 24 months vs 74% on standard-of-care.
FDA also approved the subcutaneous combination of pembrolizumab and berahyaluronidase alfa-pmph (Keytruda Qlex) plus belzutifan.

stories.headline: France replaces Palantir at DGSI with ChapsVision; €655M sovereign-AI plan, Mistral assistant for 1M state agents

key_facts.fact: French PM Sébastien Lecornu announced on June 16 that the DGSI domestic intelligence agency is terminating its Palantir contract and migrating to French rival ChapsVision.

The Palantir contract had been renewed for three years in December 2025 and was set to run until 2028 before being cut short; ChapsVision was also selected by Germany's BfV in May 2026 for similar work.
France will invest an additional €655 million ($760 million) in AI through the France 2030 program, targeting infrastructure, compute, research and industrial supply chains.

France will roll out a sovereign Assistant chatbot powered by Mistral AI to about 1 million state employees (out of 2.6 million), after a 10-month pilot with 10,000 civil servants in Interior, Justice and Bercy; estimated cost is around €700,000.
Lecornu framed the moves as a sovereignty bid: 'We must use our own AI models; we cannot accept new strategic dependencies in the digital sphere... France must have its own tools.'

stories.headline: G7 leaders convene in Évian, France with Iran deal and Ukraine on the agenda

key_facts.fact: The 2026 G7 Leaders' Summit opened in Évian-les-Bains, France on June 15 and runs through June 17, hosted by French President Emmanuel Macron in his final summit as head of state.
Canada, France, Germany, Italy and the United Kingdom issued a joint statement on the US-Iran deal announced earlier that day.
Canada is not expecting a traditional joint communique; G7 host countries are instead moving to issue-specific standalone statements endorsed by certain leaders.
Outreach country leaders from Brazil, Egypt, India, Kenya, South Korea, Qatar and the UAE are also participating.

Canadian PM Carney's Tuesday June 16 schedule includes bilateral meetings with Italian PM Meloni, Ukrainian President Zelensky, UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed, Indian PM Modi and Korean President Lee Jae Myung.
France, the UK and Italy could carry out military measures within days of the formal Iran deal signing to help commercial shipping operate and clear mines in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: Google commits $1.5B to expand Alabama data center, pledging to cover power costs

key_facts.fact: Google announced on June 15 that it will spend $1.5 billion across 2026 and 2027 to expand its Jackson County, Alabama data center campus.
Google said it will pay for 100% of the power it uses and cover infrastructure costs directly driven by the Jackson County expansion, in line with the US Ratepayer Protection Pledge.

The expansion will eventually be powered by advanced nuclear via Google's 2025 partnership with Kairos Power and TVA, supplying up to 50 megawatts of clean power to data centers in Alabama and Tennessee.

Google has contracted more than 300 MW of new generation capacity to the Tennessee Valley region; the Kairos Power Hermes 2 SMR is scheduled to begin operations in 2030, with broader 500 MW capacity targeted by 2035.
The campus has operated since 2019 on the site of TVA's retired Widows Creek coal plant in Jackson County, Alabama.

stories.headline: GPU infrastructure marketplace Hydra Host raises $100M Series A backed by Nvidia

key_facts.fact: Hydra Host announced on June 15 that it bagged $100 million in a Series A round of funding led by Kindred Ventures.
Investors in the round include Nvidia, Ark Invest, SPLY Capital, Era Funds, Comcast Ventures, Magnetar, Peak6, Founders Fund, 10x Founders, Sterling Road and Flume Ventures.
Hydra Host runs a marketplace connecting developers and enterprises to high-performance GPUs pooled from data center operators globally, aiming to ease the compute capacity crunch.
The Boulder, Colorado-based company says its Brokkr AI Factory Operating System has been deployed at more than 50 data centers across the Americas, Asia Pacific and EMEA.
CEO Aaron Ginn said the funds will expand the GPU-as-a-service platform and the company's data center footprint, with the mission of 'converting megawatts into tokens.'

stories.headline: Intellia's CRISPR therapy lonvo-z cuts HAE attacks 87% in Phase 3, BLA filing underway

key_facts.fact: Intellia's Phase 3 HAELO trial of lonvoguran ziclumeran (lonvo-z) for hereditary angioedema showed an 87% reduction in mean monthly attacks vs placebo during weeks 5-28.
62% of lonvo-z patients were attack-free and therapy-free during weeks 5-28, compared with 11% on placebo.
Mean monthly attacks requiring on-demand treatment fell 89% — 0.19 in the lonvo-z arm vs 1.79 on placebo.
All treatment-emergent adverse events in the lonvo-z arm were mild or moderate; no serious adverse events were observed.
Intellia initiated a rolling BLA submission for lonvo-z with the FDA in April; the company anticipates US approval and launch in the first half of 2027.

stories.headline: Nvidia sells $25B in first bond offering since 2021 with $85B in investor demand

key_facts.fact: Nvidia priced $25 billion of high-grade bonds on Monday, June 15, joining a wave of jumbo debt offerings from tech heavyweights tied to AI investment.
Investor demand reached approximately $85 billion, more than three times the size of the bond, and the offering was boosted from an initial target of $20 billion.
It is Nvidia's first investment-grade bond market access in five years; its previous raise was $5 billion in June 2021.

Nvidia said the proceeds will go to general corporate purposes, including repayment and refinancing of outstanding notes; sources said the main reason was to establish a liquid benchmark for its cost of credit rather than to fund capex.

The notes were sold in seven parts with maturities ranging from two to 30 years; the offering is expected to be at least four times larger than each of Nvidia's two previous debt offerings, in 2020 and 2021.
Nvidia capped the bond issue at $25 billion to keep credit spreads low, contrasting with hyperscalers funding AI infrastructure investments.

stories.headline: OpenAI's audited 2025 financials: $34B in costs on $13B revenue, $38.5B net loss

key_facts.fact: OpenAI spent $34 billion in 2025 on $13 billion in revenue, including $19.18 billion on research and development and $5.73 billion on sales and marketing, per audited financial documents reviewed by the Financial Times.
OpenAI's 2025 net loss attributable to the company was $38.5 billion, up roughly 8x from a $5.09 billion net loss in 2024.
The 2025 loss was inflated by a $41.55 billion non-cash charge tied to the fair-value re-mark of convertible interests and warrant liabilities from the for-profit conversion.
OpenAI paid Microsoft $17.2 billion in 2025, including $10.59 billion classified as R&D — largely the cost of training OpenAI's models — and received $303 million from Microsoft.
SoftBank paid OpenAI $867 million in 2025.
OpenAI confidentially filed for an IPO with the SEC last week.

stories.headline: OpenRouter launches Fusion, a multi-model deliberation API matching Fable-5 on deep research

key_facts.fact: OpenRouter launched Fusion, a 'compound model' API that fans a prompt out to a panel of AI models in parallel, has a judge model produce a structured analysis, then a synthesizer writes the final answer.

On OpenRouter's internal benchmark of 100 hard DRACO deep-research tasks, a Fusion panel of Fable 5 + GPT-5.5 scored ~69%, edging combinations of Opus 4.8 + GPT-5.5 + Gemini 3.1 Pro; solo Claude Fable 5 scored ~65%.
A budget Fusion panel of Gemini 3 Flash, Kimi K2.6 and DeepSeek V4 Pro outperformed solo GPT-5.5 and solo Claude Opus 4.8 and came within 1% of Fable 5's score at roughly half Fable 5's price.
Fusion costs are the sum of all panel + judge completions; with the default 3-model 'Quality' preset (Opus, GPT, Gemini Pro) expect roughly 4–5× the cost of a single completion.
OpenRouter says roughly three-quarters of Fusion's performance gain comes from the synthesis step, with one-quarter from model diversity.

stories.headline: Qualcomm in talks to buy AI chip startup Tenstorrent for $8B-$10B

key_facts.fact: Qualcomm is in talks to acquire AI chip startup Tenstorrent for between $8 billion and $10 billion, per The Information citing a person with direct knowledge.
Talks are ongoing and the price could change or discussions could fall apart; it is unclear if the price includes performance-based milestone payments.
Tenstorrent was founded in 2016 and is led by chip designer Jim Keller, a former Apple chip architect who also led Tesla's autonomous-driving chip effort.
An $8B-$10B price would be a significant step up from Tenstorrent's last targeted valuation of about $3.2 billion in a roughly $800 million round earlier in the year.
Qualcomm shares fell about 1% in extended trading after the report.

stories.headline: French silicon-quantum startup Quobly closes €115M Series A backed by STMicro

key_facts.fact: Quobly announced on June 15 the closing of a €115 million Series A to accelerate the industrialization of its silicon-based quantum computers.
The round is led by Bpifrance, SEALSQ and STMicroelectronics, with participation from the European Innovation Council, Blast, ALIAD (Air Liquide Venture Capital) and Innovacom.
Quobly plans to deploy its first commercial quantum computer through the cloud by the end of 2026 under its Alloy product line.
CEO and co-founder Maud Vinet said the company has shown silicon qubits can be developed within semiconductor manufacturing processes and integrated into a system architecture.
Existing Quobly shareholders include the CEA, CNRS, Quantonation and Supernova Invest.

stories.headline: Salesforce to acquire AI customer-service platform Fin (ex-Intercom) for ~$3.6B

key_facts.fact: Salesforce signed a definitive agreement to acquire Fin, formerly Intercom, for approximately $3.6 billion, subject to customary purchase-price adjustments.
Fin's core product is an AI agent powered by its proprietary model, Apex, resolving customer queries across live chat, email, WhatsApp, SMS, phone, and Slack.
Fin says its AI Agent has resolved on average 76% of support volume end-to-end and serves more than 30,000 companies.
The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of Salesforce's fiscal year 2027 and Salesforce will not change its FY27 financial guidance.
Intercom was founded in 2011 by Eoghan McCabe, Des Traynor, Ciaran Lee and David Barrett and renamed Fin in May 2026; McCabe remains CEO post-deal.
Salesforce's largest prior acquisition was the $27+ billion Slack deal that closed in 2021.

stories.headline: SpaceX flies first Falcon 9 as a public company, deploys 1,500th Starlink of 2026

key_facts.fact: SpaceX launched the Starlink 17-54 mission from Vandenberg Space Force Base at 8:34 a.m. PDT on June 15, deploying 24 Starlink V2 Mini satellites — the first Falcon 9 flight as a publicly traded company.
Booster B1093 completed its 14th flight and landed on the drone ship 'Of Course I Still Love You', marking SpaceX's 624th booster landing.
The launch raised the active Starlink constellation to 10,660 satellites, according to tracker Jonathan McDowell; over 80% of SpaceX's 69 Falcon 9 flights this year have been Starlink missions.
SPCX shares surged 19% on their first full trading day; Ron Baron followed with a $1 billion purchase of SPCX, bringing Baron Capital's total SpaceX holdings to ~$25 billion.
SpaceX's Dragon CRS-34 cargo capsule is set to depart the International Space Station on June 16.

stories.headline: Texas governor issues disaster declaration for 101 counties as Houston floods

key_facts.fact: Texas Governor Greg Abbott issued a disaster declaration for 101 counties on June 15, including Harris County, as severe storms and flooding threatened the state.
Flooding hit Greater Houston on June 15; floodwaters closed parts of Interstate 45, the University of Houston Downtown campus including its food bank, and stranded vehicles under bridges.
Abbott directed the Texas Division of Emergency Management to activate additional resources and implement 24-hour operations at the State Emergency Operations Center.
Harris County Emergency Management Director Mark Sloan warned residents the danger was 'far from over' with more heavy rain expected overnight into June 16.
Separately in California, the Shore Fire near Calimesa in Riverside County grew to 1,500 acres by 8 p.m. June 15, forcing evacuations and shutting down Highway 60 westbound.
In Washington state, the Twin Sisters Fire south of Wallula Junction grew to 8,262 acres by June 15 amid a red flag warning for central and eastern Washington and northeast Oregon.

stories.headline: Ukraine drone strike hits Moscow's largest oil refinery, 15 km from the Kremlin

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian drones struck the Moscow Oil Refinery in the Kapotnya district on the morning of June 16, igniting a fire roughly 15 kilometers from the Kremlin and about 500 km from Ukrainian-held territory.
Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 25 drones were destroyed over the city; one damaged a facility at the Moscow Oil Refinery, with no casualties reported.
Zelensky framed the strike as a 'just response' to Russian attacks and said the SBU, Unmanned Systems Forces, Special Operations Forces and military intelligence (HUR) were involved.

Russia attacked Ukraine overnight with two Iskander-M ballistic missiles and 132 drones from the evening of June 15; Ukrainian air defenses destroyed or jammed 114 of the drones, with hits at nine locations.
The strike hit the refinery's ELOU AVT-6 primary crude-distillation unit, the capital's largest refinery, located inside Russia's densest air-defense belt.
Drone strikes on Russian refineries have doubled since the start of 2026, leading to full or partial shutdowns and a decline in gasoline, diesel and jet fuel production.
